study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Floris et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Atypical Brain Asymmetry in Autism - A Candidate for Clinically Meaningful Stratification

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the study aims: to move beyond mean group comparisons by applying normative modeling to gray-matter laterality to dissect heterogeneity in autism, model individual deviations across age, and assess clinical relevance (e.g., relationships to language delay and symptom severity). This satisfies both criteria: explicit research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling for clinically meaningful stratification.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We derived gray matter voxelwise laterality values for each subject and modeled individual deviations from the normative pattern of brain laterality across age using normative modeling." | "The present study was designed to address heterogeneity in autism ... by applying normative modeling ... and to identify laterality-related subtypes by considering co-occurring clinical symptoms such as language development."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using neurotypical (NT) participants from EU-AIMS LEAP. Eligibility/exclusions and image quality criteria are described: exclude missing T1, low image quality (motion, coverage, abnormalities), failed preprocessing; exclude NTs with positive ADHD screen; restrict analyses to 5 sites after QC. Final NT sample size used to estimate the normative model is reported (N=233).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we excluded participants with missing T1-weighted MRI scans, low image quality (i.e., structural brain abnormality, excessive head motion, insufficient coverage), and failed image preprocessing. ... Neurotypical controls scoring positively for ... ADHD ... were also excluded." | "Due to low number of participants from the Rome site after quality control, we restricted analyses to the five remaining sites." | "Thus, the normative model can be estimated solely based on the neurotypical cohort (N=233), and avoids enrichment for autism."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Floris2021_sup.pdf.md, Participants/design/exclusion; Floris2021_sup.pdf.md, Gaussian process regression section

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates include age, sex, and site in the normative model for NTs. Site effects are addressed both by including site as a covariate and via a control analysis using ComBat harmonization.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "we trained a Gaussian process regression model at each voxel on the neurotypical cohort using age, sex, and site as covariates" | "We estimated a separate normative model without including site as a covariate, but removing site effects using ComBat."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Floris2021.pdf.md, Methods; Floris2021.pdf.md, Robustness and Replicability

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference (NT) cohort data source is specified as EU-AIMS LEAP, with counts for NT and ASD, and replication using ABIDE is described elsewhere.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we used the large EU-AIMS ... Longitudinal European Autism Project dataset comprising 352 individuals with autism and 233 neurotypical control subjects ..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary data collection is described with modality/subtype (structural MRI, T1-weighted), acquisition parameters (1.2 mm thickness, 1.2x1.2 mm in-plane), and equipment/manufacturer/field strength details across sites (3T scanners from Siemens, GE, Philips).
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "All participants were scanned with a contemporary MRI scanner operating at 3T at 5 different sites (University of Cambridge: Siemens Verio; King's College London: GE Medical Systems Discovery MR 750; Mannheim University: Siemens TimTrio; Radboud University: Siemens Skyra; Rome University: GE Medical Systems Signa HDxTt; Utrecht University: Philips ...)." | "High-resolution structural T1-weighted volumetric images were acquired ... at 1.2-mm thickness with 1.2x1.2-mm in-plane resolution."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is detailed: CAT12 toolbox laterality pipeline, symmetric tissue probability maps, reflection across midline, DARTEL template creation/registration, modulation to retain local volume, voxelwise laterality index computation, and smoothing. Quality control is also described in the supplement.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Structural T1-weighted images were preprocessed according to a validated laterality pipeline ... using the CAT12 toolbox (neuro.uni-jena.de/cat/). All original images were segmented and affine registered to a symmetrical tissue probability map before being reflected across the cerebral midline ... used to generate a symmetrical study-specific template via ... DARTEL ... An intensity modulation step was included ... A laterality index was calculated at each voxel ... Laterality images were smoothed with a 4-mm ... kernel." | "Consistent image quality was ensured by a semi-automated quality control procedure."
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: Floris2021.pdf.md, Image Preprocessing; Floris2021_sup.pdf.md, MRI data acquisition/QC

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They used 10-fold cross-validation within neurotypical individuals to assess generalizability and avoid overfitting before retraining on all NTs to predict ASD.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To avoid overfitting, assess generalizability, and determine whether neurotypical individuals fall within the normative range, we used 10-fold cross-validation in neurotypical individuals before retraining the model in the entire sample to make predictions in individuals with autism."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: While the study tested replicability in ABIDE, it did not apply the EU-AIMS-derived normative model to an independent external sample of healthy individuals. Instead, ABIDE data were preprocessed and normative modeling was performed in that dataset "in accordance" with the primary analysis, indicating a new model rather than external validation of the original reference model.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To assess replicability, we selected a sample from ... ABIDE I and II ... T1 images were preprocessed with the same pipeline ... Next, normative modeling and the creation of normative probability maps were done in accordance with the primary imaging analysis ..."
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.location: Floris2021.pdf.md, Robustness and Replicability; Floris2021_sup.pdf.md, ABIDE methods

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is clearly described: voxelwise Gaussian process regression with age, sex, site covariates; kernel combines linear and nonlinear terms with ARD; hyperparameters learned by maximizing log evidence; subject-level Z images computed. However, software/libraries used for normative modeling are not explicitly specified (no toolkit/version named).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Gaussian process regression was used to estimate separate normative models of grey matter laterality at each voxel ... combining linear and nonlinear terms ... automatic relevance determination ... Training ... by maximizing the logarithm of the model evidence ... Finally, we compute a single subject Z-statistic image for each subject ..." | "we trained a Gaussian process regression model at each voxel ... using age, sex, and site as covariates"
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Floris2021_sup.pdf.md, Gaussian process regression; Floris2021.pdf.md, Methods

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Although cross-validation was performed and figures reference a "positive correlation map between true and predicted values", the paper does not report quantitative model fit metrics (e.g., explained variance, correlation coefficients, RMSE) for the NT reference cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "These are based on the normative model maps thresholded with the positive correlation map between true and predicted values." (no numerical metrics reported)

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: While 10-fold cross-validation was used, the study does not report sample sizes or demographics for each partition (e.g., training/validation/test folds).
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "we used 10-fold cross-validation in neurotypical individuals ..." (no details on per-partition characteristics)
